strings.name: Lei Jun
strings.summary: A Wuhan University graduate, Lei worked in software and management at Kingsoft before founding Joyo and becoming an investor. In 2010 he co-founded Xiaomi with a team, combining smartphones, connected hardware and internet services, and took the company public in Hong Kong in 2018. He announced entry into electric vehicles in 2021 and launched the SU7 in 2024. Expansion also brought safety scrutiny; responsibility for accidents and technology requires investigative evidence.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones verifiable through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He founded Xiaomi and participated in software and smart hardware entrepreneurship, advancing smartphones, consumer IoT and the emerging manufacturing ecosystem.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Wuhan University, 1991.
strings.facts.f2.label: Birth information
strings.facts.f2.value: Born in December 1969; month precision follows the company biography.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Consumer electronics and internet
strings.highlights.h1.text: He co-founded Xiaomi, combining phones, connected devices and services in a business serving international markets.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Entry into electric vehicles
strings.highlights.h2.text: He led Xiaomi from an EV plan to SU7 sales; product safety and reliability remain subject to ongoing scrutiny.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Updates SU7 line
strings.timeline.t1.text: He launched the new-generation SU7; company claims emphasized safety and driving upgrades but alone did not establish their real-world effectiveness.
strings.timeline.t2.title: SU7 orders open
strings.timeline.t2.text: He presented the SU7, Xiaomi’s first production car, and its prices; orders opened in China that day.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Announces smart EV business
strings.timeline.t3.text: Xiaomi announced a wholly owned smart EV subsidiary with Lei concurrently serving as its CEO.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Xiaomi lists in Hong Kong
strings.timeline.t4.text: Xiaomi listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange’s Main Board; Lei attended as founder and CEO.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Co-founds Xiaomi
strings.timeline.t5.text: He founded Xiaomi with a team, subsequently developing smartphones, connected hardware and internet services.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Founds Joyo
strings.timeline.t6.text: He founded the online retailer Joyo, which Amazon acquired in 2004.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Kingsoft
strings.timeline.t7.text: He joined Kingsoft, later held senior management positions and became board chairman in 2011.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes university degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned a computer science bachelor’s degree at Wuhan University before his software, entrepreneurial and investment career.
